purpose: Pre-data code-hash records for the trainer changes made between Nov 27 7:20 PM and Nov 28 5:03 AM CT, 2026. The code itself is not in this repository. Each record was written before any run that used the changed code produced data, and it was approved by Blake Jones (rulings t250u and t251u). Only SHA-256 values and descriptions are published here. Local paths are removed. File names are kept except for the trainer main script and its corpus-hypergraph wrapper, which are named by role.

records.kvreg_fix: The assert at kvreg_model.py line 166 (register batch must match the eval micro-batch) fired because the wrapper ran the registers-OFF evaluation while the model still held the registers of the last training micro-batch (6 rows) against an eval micro-batch of 16. Root cause was the caller, not kvreg_model.py. Fix: call set_regs(None) before that ablation eval, which is what registers-off means. Slicing or expanding the stale registers would have fed unrelated training-window registers to eval windows, so kvreg_model.py and its assert are unchanged (hash identical). The canonical registers-ON eval already builds per-window causal registers.
records.gpu1_fp32: Eval-only runs (--steps 0 --ckpt) on the GTX 1660 Ti run in fp32 (autocast disabled for that process), eval micro-batch 4, and skip the GPU-0 idle wait. Every other CUDA run still asserts the RTX 5070. e2_knnlm.py on the 1660 Ti: fp32, no GPU-0 idle wait, temperature read from the 1660 Ti by name; the 5070 path and its assert are unchanged. Result JSONs gain `device` and `eval_dtype`.

records.summary: Per Blake's ruling t251u: the legacy paired second arm (sw40k) is dropped from the r2-kneg3 and r2-shrunk-resid plans, which test a single hnt40k arm against completed baselines. The tokenizer preflight rule is unchanged (not relaxed). The plans are routed to the existing single-arm launch path by changing the plan source label, with no supervisor code change. The primary-arm command line is identical to the earlier launches apart from the arm label suffix. Separately, the FLOP cross-check tool (measurement only, never part of training) was fixed: it built the model without the counts, shrink, k_neg and struct-head options the trainer passes, so the shrunk-resid probe raised an error and the k_neg probe undercounted. After the fix a CPU check of both plans measured status ok.
